title: 4 months and 540 commits with Claude: our first game, a ROUNDS-inspired arena shooter
author: DenPixelDev
selftext:
Back to Scrap is our first game, a 2D arena shooter for 2-6 players inspired by ROUNDS, already up on Steam for wishlists. Lose a round, draft an upgrade card, and the robots that die break into scrap that stays on the map.  
  
We really got going in August, about 540 commits since then. The agent wrote all the code, almost all the visuals (they're drawn as code, not generated images: the robots, the skins and the card icons are svg or python that it writes and we judge by eye), the localization into 8 languages, and even our tools: a little browser studio where we make sounds out of CC0 recordings, and the game films its own trailer takes.  
  
The idea and game design are on us. We play every build and tell the agent what's off, and a critic agent reviews every change.  
  
A couple of things we learned the hard way. The agent kept drawing robot hands wrong until we made it look up real hand poses first, and Fable 5.2 did them best. And it's better to have the AI build tools than assets: one script that draws every card icon by our rules beats dozens of one-off pictures.  
  
The video is our trailer, all of it filmed by the game itself. Steam page if you're curious: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5609690/Back\_to\_Scrap/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5609690/Back_to_Scrap/)  
  
Curious how others handle this: does anyone let their agent judge how the game looks and feels, or do you still check everything yourself in the game like we do?

comments.author: hejyhej
comments.body: Reminds me of duck game or soldat

replies.author: DenPixelDev
replies.body: Ha, I'll take it, Duck Game is a classic. Never played Soldat though, gonna check it out. Ours leans more on the ROUNDS side: lose a round and you pick an upgrade card, so by the end of a match everyone's build gets pretty weird.
